title: Thousands march in Bordeaux against cost of living and for public services
seoTitle: Bordeaux march against cost of living

tea.why: Protesters marched to express dissatisfaction with the rising cost of living, declining purchasing power, and the state of public services.
tea.want: Participants demanded improved purchasing power, better funding for public services, and support for youth and education.
tea.changed: Nov 5: A large-scale demonstration took place in Bordeaux, followed by reports of clashes between some participants and police.

summary: On November 5, 2026, a significant demonstration occurred in Bordeaux, France, as part of a broader national movement against the rising cost of living. Organised by an inter-union coalition, the march drew a large crowd, including students, teachers, healthcare workers, and retirees. Participants voiced concerns over economic hardship, the quality of educational facilities, and the need for better social protections. While the march proceeded calmly for most of the day, some sources reported clashes between protesters and law enforcement following the event's conclusion at Place de la Victoire. Estimates of the turnout varied significantly, with the prefecture reporting 21,000 participants, while the CGT union estimated 120,000. The protest was part of a series of mobilisations that continued in the city throughout the week.
demands: Better support for youth and education
response: The prefecture authorised the march route while implementing security measures to protect businesses. Following the event, the Ministry of the Interior denied allegations regarding the use of sound cannons against protesters during subsequent demonstrations.

crowd.text: The CGT estimated 120,000 participants, while the prefecture reported 21,000.

updates.text: A large demonstration against the cost of living took place in Bordeaux with varying turnout estimates.
A subsequent protest was held in Bordeaux, following a route authorised by the prefecture.
The Ministry of the Interior denied claims that sound cannons were used against protesters during the November 7 event.
